feed.title: Pronounce — recent dictionary additions
feed.subtitle: How engineers actually pronounce project / product / jargon names. Community-maintained.

entry.title: Ampersand — am per sand
entry.summary: Ampersand is pronounced "am per sand" (/ˈæmpərˌsænd/). humans&'s first collaborator model (Oct 2026, Agents API); named after the & character, ordinary English reading.

entry.title: TutorMoments — tutor moments
entry.summary: TutorMoments is pronounced "tutor moments" (/ˈtuːtər ˌmoʊmənts/). Ai2 benchmark scoring AI tutors on real tutoring decision moments; plain English compound tutor + moments.

entry.title: MegaMoE — MEG uh em oh EE
entry.summary: MegaMoE is pronounced "MEG uh em oh EE" (/ˈmɛɡə ˌɛm oʊ ˈiː/). Distributed MoE decode kernel from humans& (in FlashInfer and SGLang); mega + MoE, inheriting MoE's spelled-out vs "moh" split.

entry.title: 4-bitter Lesson — four bitter lesson
entry.summary: 4-bitter Lesson is pronounced "four bitter lesson" (/ˌfɔːrˈbɪtər ˈlɛsən/). humans& pun on Sutton's Bitter Lesson for its 4-bit RL recipe; reads four-BIT-ter LESS-un.

entry.title: Multi-User Turing Test — mul tee yoo zer touring test
entry.summary: Multi-User Turing Test is pronounced "mul tee yoo zer touring test" (/ˌmʌlti ˌjuːzər ˈtʊrɪŋ ˌtɛst/). humans&'s user-model eval where an LLM judge tells all-human group chat from simulated; Turing as TOOR-ing.

entry.title: NVFP4 — N V F P four
entry.summary: NVFP4 is pronounced "N V F P four" (/ˌɛn viː ɛf piː ˈfɔr/). NVIDIA's 4-bit floating-point format (E2M1 values, E4M3 block scales) on Blackwell/Rubin; read letter-by-letter like other precision initialisms.

entry.title: Astra — astruh
entry.summary: Astra is pronounced "astruh" (/ˈæstrə/). OpenAI's GPT-6 flagship family (Sep 2026); Latin for star, anglicized AS-truh like astral, with the Latin AH-strah as the alternate.

entry.title: DeepInfer — deep infer
entry.summary: DeepInfer is pronounced "deep infer" (/ˈdiːp ɪnˌfɜːr/). DeepSeek's open-source large-scale inference framework (Oct 2026); said as the ordinary words "deep" + "infer".

entry.title: Jev — jev
entry.summary: Jev is pronounced "jev" (/dʒɛv/). TypeSafe AI's decision model; the launch FAQ derives it from economist William Stanley Jevons, so one syllable "jev".

entry.title: Postman — post man
entry.summary: Postman is pronounced "post man" (/ˈpoʊstˌmən/). API platform named for the mail carrier; ordinary English compound POHST-man.

entry.title: Miles — miles
entry.summary: Miles is pronounced "miles" (/maɪlz/). RadixArk's open-source RL post-training framework; the README tagline confirms the ordinary English word reading.

entry.title: CooperBench — cooper bench
entry.summary: CooperBench is pronounced "cooper bench" (/ˈkuːpər ˌbɛntʃ/). Stanford/SAP benchmark scoring AI coding agents as teammates; ordinary English compound Cooper + bench.

entry.title: Four Over Six — four over six
entry.summary: Four Over Six is pronounced "four over six" (/fɔːr ˈoʊvər ˌsɪks/). NVFP4 block-scaling technique (caps block maxima at ±4 vs FP8's ±6); creators spell it as plain English words, read literally.

entry.title: T3Code — tee three code
entry.summary: T3Code is pronounced "tee three code" (/ˌtiː ˈθriː ˈkoʊd/). "tee-three-code" — every official surface renders the name letter+digit ("T3 Code", CLI `t3`, winget T3Tools.T3Code, iOS listing "T3 Code: Remote Claude & More"); sibling brand T3 Chat is likewise spoken "T three". Not "tee-cubed".

entry.title: claude-mem — clawed MEM
entry.summary: claude-mem is pronounced "clawed MEM" (/ˌklɔːd ˈmɛm/). Two spoken words: "clawed MEM". 'mem' said as a word (like Memcached, mem0), not spelled M-E-M. Persistent-memory plugin for coding agents; the creator's naming doc fixes "Claude-Mem" as the prose form.

entry.title: stroq — strock
entry.summary: stroq is pronounced "strock" (/strɑk/). Creator knocked out the obvious reading on the launch thread (q: "is it pronounced, like, stroke?" — creator: "oh no, I hadn't made that connection until now"); Kazakh Latin q = /k/, giving "strock". No official ruling; "stroke" is still the widespread default reading.

entry.title: physicl — fiz ih kul
entry.summary: physicl is pronounced "fiz ih kul" (/ˈfɪzɪkəl/). Physicl Studio — synthetic-data platform for physical AI / world models / robot training; $10M seed led by Inovia (TechCrunch, 2026-11-06). Name is 'physical' with the vowels dropped (Flickr-style), said exactly like "physical".

entry.title: SpAItial — SPAY shul
entry.summary: SpAItial is pronounced "SPAY shul" (/ˈspeɪʃəl/). Spatial-AI startup (TUM professor Matthias Niessner); Echo-3 model shipped week of 2026-11-02; early customer of Physicl (TechCrunch, 2026-11-06). Brand is the ordinary word 'spatial' with decorative AI caps inserted — NOT "spay-ai-tial".

entry.title: MaxxBench — MAKS bench
entry.summary: MaxxBench is pronounced "MAKS bench" (/ˈmæks ˌbɛntʃ/). Benchmark for task adaptation and generalization in frontier coding agents (unlap.ai, Nov 2026). The double-x is decorative: "max bench", not "maxx".

entry.title: benchmaxxing — bench maks ing
entry.summary: benchmaxxing is pronounced "bench maks ing" (/ˈbɛntʃˌmæksɪŋ/). Coined in the MaxxBench research post for grinding agent benchmark scores as an end in itself — the -maxxing suffix reads like "vibe coding"'s cousin: "bench-MAX-ing".

entry.title: mitmproxy — mid-um proxy
entry.summary: mitmproxy is pronounced "mid-um proxy" (/ˈmɪdəmˌprɑːksi/). Core team says it as one word, "midemproxy" (middle syllable reduces to schwa); Hils says it at youtu.be/hPuOtJbxJT8 0:15. Outsiders default to spelling out M-I-T-M — "mitm now stands for mitmproxy in the middle".

entry.title: Kiri — KEE-ree
entry.summary: Kiri is pronounced "KEE-ree" (/ˈkiːri/). Rust container runtime replacing Docker Desktop/OrbStack (runkiri.com). Name is the Igbo word ntakịrị, "small", per the creator README — so KEE-ree, not KIH-ree or KERRY.

entry.title: Toit — toy-t
entry.summary: Toit is pronounced "toy-t" (/tɔɪt/). ESP32 language/runtime by ex-V8/Dart engineers. Asked how to say it, the creator answered: "It's from Austin Powers. 'toit like a tiger'" — rhymes with height, not French "twah".

entry.title: Le Chonk — luh chongk
entry.summary: Le Chonk is pronounced "luh chongk" (/lə ˈtʃɑŋk/). Mistral's own nickname for Mistral Large 4 (1T params): "Unofficially ML4, very officially: le Chonk." Le as in the sibling product Le Chat (luh), matching the meme spelling chonk.

entry.title: PRQL — PREE-kwul
entry.summary: PRQL is pronounced "PREE-kwul" (/ˈpriːkwəl/). Pipelined Relational Query Language — pronounced "prequel", per the project itself, not P-R-Q-L.
